root_cause.text: In the AMD DRM HDCP 2.x HDMI repeater authentication path, `mod_hdcp_read_rx_id_list()` used the sink-reported `rx_id_list_size` directly as the I2C read length into the fixed-size `hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list` buffer, allowing an oversized ReceiverID list to overflow the buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the read call in `drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/modules/hdcp/hdcp_ddc.c` from `hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list_size` to `MIN(hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list_size, sizeof(hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list))`, and the CVE text states the 10-bit RxStatus message size field could exceed `rx_id_list[177]`, causing an out-of-bounds write during the I2C read.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clamp the HDCP receiver ID list read length to the destination buffer size to prevent overflow.
intent_record.what: The call to read() in mod_hdcp_read_rx_id_list() was changed so the length argument is no longer hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list_size alone; it now uses MIN(hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list_size, sizeof(hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list)) instead.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now caps the number of bytes read into rx_id_list to the actual size of the destination buffer, preventing an oversized read request from exceeding the array bounds and avoiding potential memory corruption.
